ANTI-ZUMA MARCHES

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
South Africans united in a call for President Zuma to step down

Unique Selling Point:
News of the week

Summary:
We cover the protests around the country - speaking to political analysts and interested party about the Anti-Zuma protest action.

Further information:
Will these marches make a difference?

We interview Prinche MAshele, Ralph Makthengka for perspective. We speak to Kebby Maphatsoe about the MK Vets stance on the protests and their decision to guard Luthuli House.

We go on the march route speaking to ordinary South Africans.

And ask just impact the marches will have on the future of South Africa and President Zuma's final stretch as leader of the ANC and the country.

STRUCTURE ANTI-ZUMA MARCHES

VO: The last couple of days have been rough for South Africans – first the midnight cabinet shuffle, then not one but two downgrades that saw the rand losing value at a dramatic rate.

PRINCE: Writing is on the wall – South African fed up.

VO: On Friday South Africans took the streets across the country. Thousands of people made their way down to Durban’s promenade … in Cape Town they marched on parliament… while thousands more took their dissatisfaction to the Union Buildings in Pretoria. Smaller groups came out in Welkom, Knysna and suburbs of Johannesburg.

LINK: South AFricans from different walks of life have united at various points across the country and here at church square in Pretoria – the one thing that they are united in is that Zuma must go.

VO: Political Analyst Prince Mashele says this has been coming.

PRINCE: Dealing with a democratically elected president that has gone rogue and he still has organisations that support – are defending…

VO: Organisations like the Umkhonto we Sizwe Military VETERANs Association, are challenging the validity of these protests. Kebby Maphatsoe is their national chairman.

KEBBY: This government is democratically elected if you want change – go vote – if you want to be a counter revolutionary – will not stand for that – we will defend for that against this revolution.

VO: As hundreds of MKM Veteran Soldiers, prepared to come up from KwaZulu Natal to guard Luthuli House and show their support for President Zuma – SAVE SA supporters started camping out in Pretoria.

LINK: Thursday, 7 pm – save sa supporters campaign out here for most of the week – let’s see what’s going on.

THEMBA: We’re here because we serious about or cause – serious about getting Jacob Zuma out.

VO: Themba Masango is one of the SAVE SA conveners – he showed us around the Church Square Camp. He says their stay has not been uneventful.

THEMBA: we were attacked by guys apparently from the youth league // People on the ground are saying they are tired, people are angry.

VO: But late on Thursday there was still confusion around the legality of the planned march to the Union Buildings and the issuing of permits – ANC Stalwart Sipho Pityana questioned the motivation behind these challenges.

SIPHO: Behind the scenes – suppress opinions & views trying to extend it – Sans must not accept it. // South Africans must not tolerate that.

VO: People were not discouraged. It’s estimated that over 100 000 South Africans showed up - young, old, bikers, people waving flags and carrying banners reflecting their dissatisfaction with President Zuma.

Organiser Ben Theron is from the civil action organisation OUTA.

BEN: Never know how much support – absolutely goosebumps but people are out all over the place – full roads – it’s rocking…

VO: They are hoping to rock the President’s boat.

BEN: We are hoping to the 400 members that represent 55 million will hear us // This is just the start.

VOXPOPS
BLACK ANC WOMAN
COLOURED MAN – JZ STEP DOWN….. you know what you are doing is wrong.

VO: But Pityana says it goes beyond the President.

SIPHO: The message is to the ANC – Pres Zuma in power because anc keep him in power – ANC members spoke out thunderously – what he doing is an assault on the ANC – He must go and he must go immediately.

UPSOUND PROTESTS

LINK: The voices here today are loud, but not angry – moving slowly through the streets of Pretoria to the union buildings.

VOX POPS
INDIAN GUY MIDDLE CLASS…
UPSOUND PROTEST - …. Can never be defeated.

VO: The power of the middle class should not be dismissed says Political Analyst Ralph Mathekga.

RALPH: History revolution comes from middle class – issues that effects the poor. Not just instigating for themselves…Russia…in a way that concern the working class.
PRINCE: People can come together and remove a sitting government. //The problem is that there is – the problem is that there is no unity from civil society – efforts are scattered and they don’t last long//

VO: On Friday, the DA held separate marches in Johannesburg, Cape Town, Durban, the Eastern Cape and the Free State.

MMUSI: // let’s get people out – one unanimous call – Zuma must go. this is about fanning across the country – across the board.

VOX POPS…. Indian Uncle…. He must go…

VO: While there was a flood of DA supporters in Johannesburg. The ANC’s MK Veterans also had around 300 combat ready members at Luthuli House.

KEBBY: If you attack the head you going to the body.
RALPH: ANC don’t need VETS – they are in government – should like that – receive memorandum and go work on it instead of trying to counter the marches.

VO: While the protests were predominantly peaceful there were some reports of violence.

Later on Friday, a group of protesters gathered at the Gupta’s family home in Saxonwold, Johannesburg.

Police eventually fired a stun grenade to disperse the crowd.

MMUSI: One person has seeded our sovereignty to one family // Not junk country // junk president.

VO: Mathekga believes protesters shouldn’t be disappointed – their actions were not wasted.

RALPH: Have arrived at point of doubt - earlier post liberation than others – good thing – if citizens have doubt about political elite – will hold them accountable – positive – give credit to JZ for pushing us faster than we ever imagined.

VO: But not fast enough for South Africans who are running out credit.

SIPHO: The ANC has to choose between the people and JZ – for as long as JZ is in power – this movement will grown in members and make sure that we are heard.


















PROMOS
PROMO 1 – 10 seconds
VO: Thousands of took to the streets calling for President Zuma to step down.

SIPHO: What he doing is an assault on the ANC – He must go and he must go immediately.

PROMO 2
VO: While calls for President Zuma to step down may not deliver immediate results – the efforts are not wasted.

RALPH: Have arrived at point of doubt - earlier post liberation than others – I think we are on the right course.

PROMO 3
VO: Thousands of South Africans came out in Anti-Zuma protests across the country - just how effective was the movement?

PRINCE: The problem is that there is no unity on the part of civil society.
